requirements.statement: Every party picker lists addresses in a table with a radio column (header 'Select', visually hidden), Name, Address and Country columns, and a last column for the row's action (header 'Actions', visually hidden); each row's radio is a small radio named after the answer the page collects, valued with the address-book record's id, and labelled 'Select <name>' in visually hidden text, so one address at most can be chosen.

requirements.statement: Every party picker's Address column shows each street line on its own line, with the town or city, county and postcode together on the line below, and leaves out any part the record does not hold; the country sits in its own column.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 prints one line per address line, which reads more easily in a narrow column. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants the same address lines in the same increment.

requirements.statement: Each animals picker row ends with a 'View' link, named 'View <name>' to a screen reader, that opens that address in the INS address book and comes back to the same picker with the search term, the trail and the chosen row as they were. This is the animals pickers' change only: the high-risk plants frontend is not wired to the INS address book, so its pickers keep their 'View details' disclosure.

requirements.statement: Reopening a picker for a party that already holds an address picked from the book ticks that address's radio and names it in the inset; a copy whose record has gone from the book, been deleted, or is not offered for the picker's role opens with nothing ticked and the held copy still shown. A selection named in the address wins over the one the notification holds.
requirements.why: The prototype pre-selects the current choice, and both real pickers already do.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-043 shows the chosen row ticked once its page is shown and repo-tests-p7-077 a deleted record dropped with nothing ticked; repo-plantsfrontend-p9-060 to -p9-062, -p9-074 and -p9-078 show the same in plants, with a selection in the address winning over the stored one.

requirements.statement: Pressing 'Save and continue' on a party picker with no address chosen shows no error, leaves the party as it was — empty, or holding its earlier address as the trader edited it — and moves the trader on as a valid save would, an animals picker to the consignment addresses page and a plants picker to the next page of its journey or to the overview. The save is logged once as committing nothing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader leave a picker without choosing; completeness is checked by the task status and the review, not by the picker. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants' pickers the same lenient blank save, and the owner's 26 October ruling makes plants' 'Save and return to overview' check exactly what its 'Save and continue' checks, so both of its buttons are lenient.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-050 shows an animals picker saved with nothing ticked returning to the consignment addresses page with that party still offering only its add link, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-065, -p9-066, -p7-080, -p7-081 and -p7-099 show plants committing nothing, raising no error, leaving an edited copy untouched and logging the save once. Before it landed both frontends re-rendered the picker with status 400 and 'Select a <party> from the list' (trace-animals-fit-p14-050 to -054).

requirements.statement: Saving a picker with an address that is not in the organisation's book, has been deleted since the page loaded, or is not offered for that picker's role saves nothing and re-renders the picker with status 400, an error summary 'There is a problem' and the picker's own error: 'Select a place of origin from the list', 'Select a consignor from the list', 'Select a consignee from the list', 'Select an importer from the list', 'Select a place of destination from the list' or 'Select a contact address from the list' and their Welsh, shown above the results with a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix, the summary link going to the first address radio or, with no rows, to the search box. The ticked row is cleared, the search term and its results stay, and the refusal is logged with the address id and the reason.
requirements.why: A real constraint the prototype cannot express: the notification must never hold a party copied from a record the organisation does not have, or does not have for that role.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-028 holds the five animals errors and repo-frontend-p14-095 treats a deleted or wrongly-roled record as never chosen; repo-plantsfrontend-p9-067 to -p9-072 show plants refusing such an id at status 400 with its own message, clearing the tick, keeping the search and logging the reason, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-037 shows the summary link going to the first row or to the search box.

requirements.statement: Outside an amendment, each of the five animals party pickers and the CPH number page end with a single primary 'Save and continue' button, with no 'Save and return to overview' button and no cancel link. While amending, each ends with the amendment's own save and return controls.
requirements.why: DR1 ruled this same difference (rule (b)): only pages the overview links to end with the three return controls, and a page reached from another page ends with the primary button alone; the animals pickers are reached from the consignment addresses page. The amendment's endings are req-1624's, in the journey-flow area.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p9-045 and trace-animals-fit-p15-030 show the animals pickers ending with 'Save and continue' alone today, and document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-057 records the CPH number page built the same way under DR1 rule (b). The permanent address page follows the same rule (req-748).

requirements.statement: Choosing an address on an animals picker and pressing 'Save and continue' saves on the notification a copy of that record — the record it came from, its name, telephone number, email address and address — and returns to the consignment addresses page, or to check your answers under change context. The page names each party from that copy, never from the address book, so renaming, moving or deleting the record afterwards leaves the notification, its review, its submitted view and its amendment as they were.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real service both save the chosen address against the party and return to the page; the copy keeps the notification stable when the book changes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-052 shows every party answer stored as a copy taken when it was chosen rather than a live reference, repo-frontend-p14-030 the return to the consignment addresses page, and repo-tests-p7-073, -p7-075, -p7-097 and -p7-100 that a later rename or deletion leaves the draft, the review, the submitted view and the amendment unchanged.

requirements.statement: If saving a picked address fails because the backend is briefly unavailable, the picker re-renders with status 500, the recoverable-error message, the trader's choice still ticked, their search term still in the box and the page of results they were on, and the failure is logged once.
requirements.why: A real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express: the trader must not lose their choice when the save fails.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-079 shows the picker shown again at status 500 with the recoverable-error banner and the choice still ticked, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-005-m1 that the page of results is honoured, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-080 that a programming failure is raised instead.

requirements.statement: Each party picker, on both animals sets and in the high-risk plants frontend, offers only the organisation's addresses whose roles include that party's role: place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer or place of destination. Its search looks only within that role, and a party filled from another party's record is not offered that record in its own picker.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 filters each picker to its role, so a trader is not offered a GB importer as a place of origin; DR1 found the unfiltered list a live defect on all the pickers, and ruling sam-2026-10-09 keeps address roles because DR1 asked for role-filtered pickers. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm builds the role-filtered pickers and gives plants the same change in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-029 binds each animals party to its address-book role so only records offered for that role can be chosen, and repo-tests-p7-038, -p7-040 and -p7-085 prove the role-filtered list, the role-scoped search and the source record not being offered after a same-as fill; repo-plantsfrontend-p7-007, -p8-023 and -p9-073 show plants' consignor and place of destination pickers asking for their own role. Before it landed all five animals pickers searched one undifferentiated book (trace-animals-fit-p14-045).

requirements.statement: The consignor picker offers addresses saved for the consignor role, including any a trader thinks of as the exporter; there is no separate exporter party and no exporter role. How the address book records those roles is the address book's design.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's consignor section covers the exporter too. Ruling ian-2026-11-16 decides that no EXPORTER role is added anywhere, because the prototype's consignor-or-exporter vocabulary is its own internal type rather than a domain role, and ruling sam-2026-10-09 leaves the field shape of address roles to the address book service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-116 and -p7-117 show the address book holding six roles — place of origin, consignor, place of destination, consignee, importer and branch address — with no exporter among them.

requirements.statement: An address saved with several roles appears on the picker of every party whose role it carries.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets one saved address be reused across parties, such as the same company as consignee and importer.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-038 shows a record saved for two roles listed on both roles' pickers.

requirements.statement: The address book holds one or more roles on each address record and lets a frontend list an organisation's live addresses for one or more roles, newest first, one page at a time, excluding deleted records: the list takes a repeatable role filter matching any of the roles given, a search-role filter, a search term and a country filter, with a 1-based page defaulting to the first and a page size of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25. The role filter runs in the service before the page is cut. The animals frontend and the high-risk plants frontend each ask for their picker's role. The record's field shape for roles is the address book service's own design, not the prototype's.
requirements.why: DR1 found role filtering needs a typed address record, which no frontend can fake, and the address book is one of this programme's repos. Ruling paul-2026-11-05 point 8 keeps pagination on the list even though the prototype has none, because organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses, and ruling ian-2026-11-25 drops this requirement's earlier 'unpaginated' clause and confirms Paul's point 8 stands in full.
requirements.deltaNote: ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-012 to -p1-018 record the service as it stands on main: a list request filters on searchTerm, countryCodes, roles and searchRoles, lists the caller's live addresses newest first one page at a time with a 1-based page and a page size of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, and cuts the page after the role filter has run. repo-tests-p7-116 and -p2-132 show the six roles held against each record, and repo-frontend-p14-029, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-073 and -p9-019 show each frontend asking for its picker's role. Collecting the roles when an address is saved is the address-book and party-address-add-and-edit areas' work.

requirements.statement: An address-book record that carries no role yet is offered on every party picker, in the animals frontend and in the high-risk plants frontend, until it is given a role, in the compose stack and in CDP alike.
requirements.why: Records saved before roles existed are a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, and DR1's judgement rules out filtering them on a guess, which would hide addresses the trader legitimately wants.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-073, -p7-008 and -p7-009 show plants' pickers offering the records that carry their own role together with those carrying no role, and no others. No claim in this working set shows how the animals pickers treat a record with no role: repo-tests-p7-038 proves only that a picker lists the addresses saved for its party's role.

requirements.statement: In stub mode, each canned address-book record carries one or more roles, in the animals frontend's stub and in the high-risk plants frontend's stub book, so the stub-mode pickers filter by role as the real ones do.
requirements.why: The stub mirrors the tests repo's address-book fixture record for record and is what local development and each frontend's own suite run against; without roles it cannot show role filtering.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants' stub book now holds roles: nine of its records are offered on the consignor picker and nine hold the destination role, while eighteen are offered on the role-free contact picker (repo-plantsfrontend-p7-009, -p8-042, -p7-073). No claim in this working set shows the animals frontend's own stub records carrying roles, and repo-tests-p2-131 records that the address book's role-driven ordering and filtering is proven only against the real service and skipped against stubs.

requirements.statement: Each party picker lists its addresses newest first, so an address just added through the address book appears at the top.
requirements.why: The prototype lists newly added addresses first, and the address book already serves its list newest first.
requirements.deltaNote: ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-013 records the address book listing the caller's live addresses newest first, one page at a time, and trace-e2e-p9-030 and -p9-031 show the newest record filling the top of page one of the picker.

requirements.statement: When a party picker has no rows to list, because a search matched nothing or because the organisation's book holds no address it offers, it shows 'No addresses match your search.' where the results count would go, renders neither the fieldset nor the table, and still offers 'Save and continue'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not draw an empty result; the real message tells the trader why the list is empty, and nothing in the prototype contradicts it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-054 and -p2-115 show the animals message today, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-021 and -p9-036-m1 the same wording in plants, shown whenever the picker has no rows rather than only after a search.

requirements.statement: Every address-book read a journey makes is made on the server, for the signed-in session's organisation only, and a record belonging to another organisation is never offered or resolved; with no organisation on the session no read is made.
requirements.why: A real authorisation constraint: the address book trusts the organisation the caller names, so the frontend's scoping is what keeps one organisation's addresses from another.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-094 scopes the read to the organisation on the trader's signed-in session so another organisation's record is never returned, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-084 scopes both the addresses offered and the record a save resolves, and trace-e2e-p9-101 shows the calls made server-side.

requirements.statement: A deleted address-book record is never offered on a picker and can never be saved, and a stored answer picked from one shows no ticked row; an address book that cannot be reached is an error, never read as a deletion.
requirements.why: Deleted addresses must not be chosen again, and an outage must not look like a deletion.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-095 treats a deleted record as never chosen, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-071 and -p9-074 keep it off the picker and show no ticked row, and repo-tests-p7-076 and -p7-077 prove the soft delete and the dropped row end to end. repo-plantsfrontend-p7-102 shows plants handling no failure at all when the address book cannot be reached while listing addresses: only a failed save of the notification is handled.

requirements.statement: A journey reads the address book and never writes to it: adding a record goes through the INS frontend, and neither journey serves a create-address page of its own.
requirements.why: The INS frontend is the address book's only writer; how Design Release 2.1's in-journey add page is met belongs to the party-address-add-and-edit area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-096 shows the live-animals addresses/create path answering 404, repo-frontend-p14-075 the hand-off out to the INS address book's add page, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-095-m1 that no plants picker offers a way to add an address the book does not hold.

requirements.statement: Every string on the consignment addresses page and on every party picker, in both frontends, has a Welsh counterpart, still marked as a machine draft awaiting translator sign-off and not to be shown to users before Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: Both real services are bilingual, and DR1 asked for each copy change in both languages; the prototype has no Welsh.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-104 shows the animals page's Welsh file carrying the same keys as the English one and marked as an unreviewed machine draft, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-086 and -p8-129 show every word the plants picker shell and the place of destination page show existing in both languages, likewise marked a machine draft (repo-plantsfrontend-p9-085, -p8-045).

requirements.statement: The consignment addresses page and every party picker, in both frontends, have no serious or critical accessibility violations against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 A and AA and 2.2 AA, on first render and in their error states, and a stored address name or address line holding markup characters is shown as text rather than rendered as markup.
requirements.why: The real pages pass today and must keep passing as they change.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p7-027, -p7-028 and -p8-044 show plants' pickers clean on first render and in their refused state, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-048 that stored markup is shown as text, and trace-animals-fit-p14-020 and -p15-037 clean axe scans of the animals page and picker.

Before that, Design Release 2.1 searched the place of origin list by country with this label and ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm built it.

requirements.why: Out of scope: the prototype itself withdrew the place of origin picker's separate country search, so the picker takes the same search hint as the other four. Before that, Design Release 2.1 gave this hint and ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm built it.

requirements.statement: The place of origin picker's search box shows the placeholder 'Search for a country'.

Without JavaScript the native select and the button do the same.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the prototype itself withdrew the place of origin picker's separate country search, so there is no country search to build. Before that, ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm built the no-JavaScript half with the accessible autocomplete, whose entries come from MDM.
requirements.deltaNote: The place of origin picker has the same free-text server search within its own role as every other picker (repo-tests-p7-040).

requirements.statement: The prototype's fixed demonstration addresses (nine places of origin, nine consignors, six consignees and importers, three places of destination) and its development socket polling are built into the real service.
requirements.why: Out of scope: they are the prototype's seed data; the real pickers list the organisation's own address book.

requirements.statement: The prototype's page paths (/roles-and-addresses, /place-of-origin, /consignor-or-exporter, /consignee, /importer, /place-of-destination under /design-release-2.1) replace the real service's routes.
requirements.why: Out of scope: ruling sam-2026-10-09 says the prototype never decides URL paths and no increment changes an existing real path to match it; the real service keeps /addresses and its /select routes, in both the live-animals and the germinal-products sets.

requirements.statement: The consignment addresses page's Change links drop the visually hidden party name, as the prototype's do.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the prototype's identical 'Change' links are an accessibility gap a sighted user cannot see, not a design choice; the real links keep naming the party for screen-reader users.

requirements.statement: The germinal-products set's consignment addresses page shows only the five party sections (Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination) for every germinal commodity: no CPH number section and no permanent address section, and the germinal set serves no CPH number or permanent address page behind them.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leaves the CPH number out for 05111000 and 05119985 and walks germinal products through five address roles only. Ruling sam-2026-10-09 makes germinal products its own set, leaves the CPH number and permanent address pages out of it, and splits req-574 so this germinal half sits in the germinal set's increment.
requirements.deltaNote: There is no germinal-products set today; germinal products run through the live-animals set, whose CPH section shows whenever the CPH number is in scope (repo-frontend-p14-059) and whose rule exempts only horses and the animals needing a permanent address (trace-animals-fit-p14-027), so 05111000 and 05119985 are asked for a CPH number.

requirements.statement: The germinal-products set has its own consignment addresses page and its own five party pickers, copied from the live-animals set's addresses feature, under the germinal set's own journey and routes with the live-animals slugs. The copy behaves as the live-animals page and pickers do in every respect but the CPH number and permanent address sections, which the germinal set does not show, and it keeps the live-animal hints word for word, including 'The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain' and the place of destination's 'unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours'.
requirements.why: Ruling sam-2026-10-09 (option B) makes germinal products a sibling set in the animals frontend whose pages are copies of their live-animals feature folders plus the prototype's germinal differences, and calls that duplication accepted and desired. Design Release 2.1 shows germinal products the same addresses page and wording as live animals. The two exceptions are req-574 and req-575, whose germinal half is req-1826.
requirements.deltaNote: The addresses page and the five pickers exist only in the live-animals set today (repo-frontend-p14-001, repo-frontend-p14-027).

requirements.statement: The consignment addresses page and the party pickers keep the routes and form fields the k6 performance scripts drive: the addresses page and the five /select pickers, the picker's search text field q submitted with action=search, the address radio saved with action=save, and a picker save landing back on the addresses page; a picker search still answers a 255-character search term.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-001 and repo-frontend-p14-027 show the addresses page and the five /select paths, repo-tests-p7-053-m1 the search posted to the picker's own /select path, and trace-animals-fit-p14-037 and -p14-061 the q field, action=search, the party radio and action=save, as repo-perftests-p1-049 drives them.

requirements.why: Out of scope: ruling sam-2026-10-09 says the prototype never decides query parameter or form field names, and kept prototype content is built without its field shape. The real pickers keep their own radio and action names, and the same-as buttons are named in the real service's conventions.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, the place of origin picker's rows filter as the trader types or picks a country, keeping the rows whose country contains the typed text or exactly matches the picked country, with no page reload, on both animals sets. It is its own waiting-on-design increment, built as design answers or dropped if design drops it.
requirements.why: Out of scope: ruling design-2026-11-13 point 2 decides that address search does not filter as the trader types; the trader presses Search or Enter, as the real service already does. Before it, Design Release 2.1 filtered the place of origin rows as the trader typed and ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm held the as-you-type half for design.
requirements.deltaNote: No picker filters its rows in the browser today: repo-tests-p7-053-m1 shows the animals search posted to the picker's own path and answered with a full page, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-082 shows the plants picker working entirely without JavaScript.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants frontend's pickers keep each row's 'View details' disclosure, named 'View details for <name>' to a screen reader, holding the record's telephone number and email address; they get no 'View' link to the INS address book.
requirements.why: Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm keeps the 'View' link to the INS address book to the animals pickers, because plants is not wired to the INS address book.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-046 and -p9-047 show the collapsed 'View details' disclosure on every plants picker row, revealing the record's telephone number then its email address and nothing else.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants frontend holds each picked party — the consignor, the place of destination and the consignment contact address — as a copy of the address-book record taken when it was picked, carrying its name, telephone number, email address and address lines in the address book's own field names, so a later change to the record does not reach the notification. The record's id is kept only to tick that row when the picker reopens, and a party with no name reads everywhere as not provided.
requirements.why: How plants stores a party is architecture, which the prototype never decides; ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm mirrors structure, wording, components and behaviour into plants while plants keeps its own data.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers keep their own questions and place in the journey.
